system.summary: 1635/1640: homophonic Latin alphabet of two-digit numbers and single letters (2-5 homophones per letter, R1889); 1640 adds a syllabary in AEIOU series: numbers 40-54 (l/n/r + vowel) and letter groups that show the vowel openly (pla..plu = ta..tu, ap..up = ca..cu, ...). 1634: a different repertoire of vowel-series letter groups (xar..xur = ta..tu, ob..ub = mo..mu, ...), numbers and graphic signs.

diacritics.note: 1634: superscript marks (9, v, x, o) change or double a sign (13^9 = ll)

system.sibling_key: R1889's alphabet (from the draft R954) is the base of R1890; R1887 shares only the vowel-series principle.
system.notes: DECODE gives R1887 as homophonic; it is a syllabic nomenclator.

prior_solution.where: Andrew Aymeloglu, github.com/aaymeloglu/unsolved-ciphers: ferdinand-1635-1640 (R1889, R1890 read, 18 Sept 2026) and ferdinand-1634 (R1887 partial, 23 Sept 2026); Tomokiyo's Unsolved list marks them Two of Three Solved. Schmeh Top 50 #27 / Thomas Ernst 2017 concern other letters (Ferdinand III to Leopold Wilhelm). Exposure: Found 30 Sept 2026, not opened. On 9 Oct, after the failed ciphertext-only R1890 run, his README and SOURCES.md were read: the README says the 1640 additions to the 1635 alphabet are mostly syllables; SOURCES.md points to the draft R954 (already on our saved DECODE record of R1889). No key value or reading came from him: KEY.md, the READING files and ferdinand-1634/ were opened only after our recovery, for comparison. The R1890 syllabary recovery was therefore made knowing that the extra symbols are mostly syllables.

solution.what: DECODE R1887/R1889/R1890 images and transcriptions need authentication; Brussels archive not online. Skipped.
Found https://github.com/aaymeloglu/unsolved-ciphers with readings of all three letters.
DECODE login cookie: fetched all 8 images of R1887/R1889/R1890, DECODE transcriptions D3605 (R1889) and D3604 (R1890), record pages R953-R955, R1885-R1892.

Schmeh Top 50 #27 / Thomas Ernst 2017 'Zifra Piccolominea' checked: concerns Ferdinand III to Archduke Leopold Wilhelm (20 July 1640 and 1641), not these Brussels letters; Ernst's key does not fit R1889/R1890. research/top50 claim is wrong for this target.
R1890 ciphertext-only homophonic anneal (symbol->letter, la 5-gram + frequency term), 16x4M and 60x10M restarts; control on synthetic 786-token Latin homophonic recovered 99.7%.
R1890 letter groups = their own vowel (pli=i, op=o ...).
Draft R954 (pointed to on the R1889 record): underlined plaintext aligned word by word with R1889's cipher; 74 words, 463 tokens; letter key with 2-5 homophones per letter.
R1890 with R1889 key fixed: free-value anneal of unknown symbols over letters/bigrams/trigrams suggested numbers in vowel series (48=no, 51=re, 53=ro ...).

R1890 family anneal: each letter-group/number family = one consonant + AEIOU vowel; all top restarts converge on the same syllabary (40s=l/n/r+v, pl?=t+v, ?p=c+v, c?=m+v, h?=d+v, t?s=b+v, ?n=s+v, ?u=p+v, m?=f+v, ?t=g+v, g?=h+v).
R1890 completed by context (ko=do, fu=mu, lx=oc, li=xi, 14=tz) and image checks of DECODE's uncertain signs (l/z?=z, c/1?o/0?=co, pla/u?=plu); all 782 tokens assigned; Latin text read in full.
After our recovery, compared with aaymeloglu/unsolved-ciphers KEY.md and READING-1640.md (18 Sept 2026): same syllabary, same singleton values, same Latin.
R1887 transcribed from the images (no DECODE transcription): 30 lines, 474 tokens, graphic signs labelled.
R1887 family anneal (consonant + shown vowel per letter-group family, rest free): collapsed to bare vowels; with consonants forced, Latin-like but not converged.
R1887 last cipher passage = the following clear words promovere haud dedignetur; fixes 5 families and 11 signs.
R1887 anneal with the crib fixed converges on the remaining families (f?r=c+v, ?c=v+s, p?n=l+v, s?l=b+v, t?s=s+v, l?s=g+v, ?r=f+v) and most signs.
R1887 read word by word with image re-checks (align1887.txt): 88.4% of tokens as sense, 93.9% with conjectures; a 6-token word and a 16-token span before negotium open.
LM span search over value options for the open 16-token R1887 span (span1887.py): fragments only.
R1887 reading compared after the fact with aaymeloglu ferdinand-1634: same families, same open spans; we add suorum and the conjectures ausus quos, eventus, quam ea.
Tomokiyo cryptiana unsolved list: Two of Three Solved (Aymeloglu, 19 Sept 2026). Hildegard Ernst MIOG 100 (1992) on these ciphers not reachable online.

Last attempt on the two open R1887 pieces (crisdus, 16-token span before negotium): every attested value per sign, group vowels fixed, pruned to la-gutenberg word segmentations and ranked by the la LM in context (gap1887.py); crops re-viewed. 571 and 1,704 candidates, none fits the sentence.
research/top50/NOTES.md and README corrected: Ernst 2017 (Top 50 #27) concerns Ferdinand III to Leopold Wilhelm 1640/41, not the Brussels letters.
